nodes.description: Store format and determinism, kg add merge rules, how kg extract updates the parser layer, kg status, kg remove and kg edit.

nodes.description: kg query (node, find, path, untested, tested, undocumented) and kg impact: options, propagation rules, coverage limits and the stable JSON output.

nodes.label: Roadmap v0.2 and v0.3
nodes.description: Action plan after the MVP: the time-boxed v0.2 evidence phase, its issue order and benchmark design, exit questions and the tentative v0.3 priorities.

nodes.label: Benchmark report
nodes.description: v0.2 decision point: graph vs. code strategies on 29 questions; the graph is as accurate but not cheaper, helps on multi-hop questions and is safe when stale.

nodes.label: Requirements discovery
nodes.description: Condensed client interview that explains why the requirements are what they are: vision, graph model, features and priorities.

nodes.label: MVP validation
nodes.description: Validation of the MVP acceptance criteria on three public repos plus kg: timings, agent enrichment, reference questions and findings.

nodes.label: Benchmark harness
nodes.description: How the bench/ harness works: strategies and tools, repos and questions, grading, metrics, the API runner and the subagent runner.

nodes.label: Rules for coding agents
nodes.description: Rules every coding agent follows in this repo: layout, environment, testing and language rules, and the reference docs to read.

nodes.label: Contributing
nodes.description: Conventional Commits with issue and RF references, branch naming, issue templates, labels and milestones.

nodes.label: No LLM inside kg
nodes.description: kg never calls an LLM nor needs API keys; external agents do the reading and send JSON, and an embedded LLM is out of scope.

nodes.label: Build on NetworkX
nodes.description: The graph is an nx.MultiDiGraph with NetworkX as the graph engine, on Python 3.12 or later.

nodes.label: Slug IDs for non-code entities
nodes.description: Entities with no physical origin use <type>:<slug> IDs, so agent knowledge merges by ID like extracted code.

nodes.label: Embed vis-network, not pyvis
nodes.description: The HTML embeds vis-network 9.1.2 with its own page; pyvis lacks filters, search and the details panel and pulls in ipython.

nodes.label: Single-file store
nodes.description: The store is one graph.json written atomically, so it is never half-written and a change only touches its own lines.

nodes.label: Parser provenance wins
nodes.description: When merging, a parser provenance is kept over an llm or manual one, so enrichment cannot wipe deterministic data; a configurable policy is RF-33 (v0.3).

nodes.label: Three hues for entity families
nodes.description: Only three hues stay distinguishable across all pairs, also with color-vision deficiencies; shape and the legend carry the type.

nodes.label: Stale graph by content digests
nodes.description: The graph records a SHA-256 digest of every file it read and kg status compares them with the disk; comparing git commits would flag a committed graph as stale forever, and digests work without git.

nodes.label: Every answer states its limits
nodes.description: kg query and kg impact end with notes on what the answer may miss (stale graph, unread files, missing relation types), because the graph never holds everything; an empty result reads 'no relation found in the graph'.

nodes.label: Impact lists possible effects
nodes.description: kg impact says 'may affect' and gives each result its relation path, depth and weakest confidence, because static relations cannot prove that a change breaks something.

nodes.label: Impact climbs containment
nodes.description: A changed function or class also changes the module that defines it, so impact reaches whatever imports that module; this stands in for the missing calls edges.

nodes.label: Filter results at query time
nodes.description: kg impact --type and kg query tested (#49) keep answers short without separate topic stores: an impact answer had 109 of 125 results as tests, and the agent ran out of calls checking tests one by one.

nodes.label: Extract replaces the parser layer
nodes.description: Every kg extract replaces the derived parser elements so the graph follows deleted, renamed and moved code, while llm and manual knowledge is kept; a failed extraction leaves the store untouched.

nodes.label: Keep derived nodes agents still use
nodes.description: A derived node the code no longer has is kept and reported while an agent or manual edge points at it, because removing it would break that edge.

nodes.label: Full rebuild before incremental
nodes.description: v0.2 rebuilds the whole parser layer on each extract (about 1 s for 100 files); processing only changed files is RF-78, deferred until full updates become slow.

nodes.label: Benchmark outside the package
nodes.description: The benchmark calls an LLM, so it lives in bench/ with its own optional dependency group; kg itself still calls no LLM (RF-24).

nodes.label: Subagent runner, no API key
nodes.description: bench.subagent runs the same questions and confined tools with subagents of a coding agent, so the benchmark needs no API key; confinement is by instruction and checked in the call log.

nodes.label: Mechanical grading, no LLM judge
nodes.description: Answers are scored with F1 over normalized names or keyword groups, so grading is reproducible; the cost is false negatives that the report corrects by reading the answers.

nodes.label: Same model for every strategy
nodes.description: Each question runs once per strategy with the same model, effort, system prompt and turn limit, and no fallback model, so the strategies differ only in their tools.

nodes.label: Topic stores from type filters
nodes.description: The topic strategy builds subsets of the full store with the RF-40 type filters instead of adding named views to kg (RF-44, v0.3), which only come if focused graphs help.

nodes.label: v0.2 is a time-boxed evidence phase
nodes.description: v0.2 measures whether the graph helps (benchmark, queries, a reliable graph, a demo) in about two weeks; extra items move to v0.3, whose scope follows the benchmark results.

nodes.label: Benchmark a large repo first
nodes.description: The v0.2 evidence only covers small repos where reading code is cheap, so v0.3 starts with a benchmark on a repo of hundreds of modules; if the graph does not win there, a redesign starts.

nodes.label: Works fully offline
nodes.description: kg works 100 % offline and sends no code or data to any service, a privacy constraint from the client interview.

nodes.label: Read-only HTML with commands
nodes.description: The HTML is a file with no server, so it cannot write to the store; it shows the matching kg edit or kg remove command to copy instead.

nodes.label: No pyplot in library code
nodes.description: Library code and tests never use pyplot or call plt.show(), which blocks; renderers return or save a matplotlib Figure.

nodes.label: Knowledge graph
nodes.description: Typed nodes and relations describing a project's code, dependencies, docs, tests and decisions, for people and AI agents.

nodes.label: Stable ID
nodes.description: An ID derived from the element's nature, so the same element always gets the same ID and merges instead of duplicating.

nodes.label: Provenance
nodes.description: Where each node and relation comes from: method, extractor, confidence, source and lines.

nodes.label: Merge by ID
nodes.description: Adding an element with an existing ID combines it with the stored one instead of duplicating it.

nodes.label: Determinism
nodes.description: The same input gives the same store and the same files, byte for byte, and the same layout with a fixed seed.

nodes.label: Change impact
nodes.description: The elements that may be affected by a change: what uses, tests, documents or justifies it, reached by walking relations backwards plus containment.

nodes.label: Coverage limits
nodes.description: Notes on what a query answer may be missing: stale_graph, freshness_unknown, unread_files and missing_relations.

nodes.label: Stale graph
nodes.description: A graph older than the code it describes: files modified, added or deleted since the last kg extract, which kg status lists and queries warn about.

nodes.label: Content digest
nodes.description: sha256: plus the first 16 hex digits of a file's SHA-256, stored in attrs.digest of File and Config nodes to tell whether the file changed.

nodes.label: Derived (parser) layer
nodes.description: The nodes and edges with method parser from kg's own extractors; kg extract owns and replaces this layer on every run.

nodes.label: Agent layer
nodes.description: Knowledge an external agent adds with kg add (documents, decisions, concepts, issues), with llm provenance; kg extract never removes it.

nodes.label: Tested criterion
nodes.description: Code counts as tested when a tests edge points to it (a test imports or refers to it directly); untested and tested split the same set.

nodes.label: Reference questions
nodes.description: The three questions kg must support: which tests are missing, is the documentation in line with the code, and how to extend the project with new requirements.

nodes.label: Benchmark strategy
nodes.description: How the agent may gather evidence in a run: code (list, read, search files), graph (read-only kg query, impact, status) or topic (the same over a topic store).

nodes.label: Topic store
nodes.description: A subset of the full store with the entity types one topic needs (development, tests, documentation, decisions) plus Repo, File and Config.

nodes.label: Traceability
nodes.description: The share of an answer's cited evidence (path:line, node IDs, edges) that exists in the repo or the graph.

nodes.label: requirements.md CLI list misses guide and schema
nodes.description: Section 5 of docs/requirements.md lists the commands without kg guide and kg schema, which the CLI has (kg.cli._guide, kg.cli._schema) and the README roadmap lists.

nodes.label: RF-20 says to iterate with kg validate
nodes.description: RF-20 tells agents to validate and iterate with kg validate, but kg guide says to use kg add --dry-run, because kg validate sees edges to extracted nodes as broken.

nodes.label: CONTRIBUTING scopes miss bench
nodes.description: CONTRIBUTING.md lists the commit scopes and area labels without bench (or update), while the benchmark commits use feat(bench) and chore(bench).
